newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-Polish grain duties raise inflation concern.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Polish grain duties raise inflation concern.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday decided to reinstate duties on most grain imports five months ahead of schedule, despite warnings from the finance minister that the move may undermine plans to slash 1997 inflation.
The timing of the move will ensure that domestic producers are able to sell grains profitably after this year's harvest, government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said.
"The move will ensure that grains elevators will not be full after the harvest," she told a news briefing. Imports of durum wheat, maize and soybeans will remain duty free, she said.
The cabinet voted to reinstate duties on other grain imports at ten percent after suspending a 20 percent tariff aimed at curbing food price rises in April 1996.
Finance minister Grzegorz Kolodko was the only cabinet member to oppose Tuesday's decision.
The duty will become effective ten days after the government publishes the decision in its official buletin due later this week, allowing importers to sign currently negotiated contracts.

Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski and his co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL), spearheaded demands to reinstate the duty, arguing the market had stabilised on substantial imports and healthy grain output prospects.
But Kolodko maintained that pressure from Jagielinski for an early end to free grains imports was motivated politically by the interest of their rural electorate.
The duty might jeopardise the government's plans to substantially curb inflation in 1997, he said. He believes that food price increases are one of the main factors fuelling Poland's inflation.
The governmment wants to cut annual average inflation to 15 percent from last year's level of close to 20 percent.
"Because of this decision the annual average 15-percent inflation goal (for 1997)...is seriously threatened. It is regrettable that the government gave in to political arguments," Kolodko.
Opposition politicians say the PSL pressed for the reinstatement of duties to ahead of the original end-June target date to boost their chances in this year's parliamentary elections.

Jukubowska said the early introduction of grain duties was unlikely to fan further inflation because the government would suspend the tarrif again as soon as grain prices start growing faster than overall consumer prices. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
